analyst_view.overall: Eibar return to league play after two weeks off, their game at Castellón having been postponed after the death of Tenerife's Jesús de Miguel (it is now set for 9 December), and they have taken two points from their last four league games. Cádiz, near the bottom after two straight defeats, are without Javi Castro (muscle injury) and Bojan Kovacevic and Kenan Toibibou, who are away with their national teams, while Gonzalo Petit and Vladyslav Kopotun are fit again. Eibar have Sergio Álvarez back after two months out but miss Gift, Elgezabal and Bernat, with Arbilla a doubt; no referee had been named in the reports I read.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals and I stay there. Eibar have scored one or none in each of their last three league games, and Borja Jiménez admits Cádiz are not creating enough to win, but both teams' league games have averaged well over two goals this season, so I do not go lower than the site.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. I lean slightly lower: Jiménez expects Ipurua to force a stop-start game of long balls, and Eibar under Jokin Aranbarri are not a side that pins teams back with long spells of possession.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards. I lean higher: Cádiz have collected yellows steadily this season, Jiménez has spent the week asking for more aggressive pressing from the back, and a reshuffled Cádiz defence (Sergio Arribas possibly moving inside) will be stretched by Eibar's direct play.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, with 17.4 for Eibar. That looks high for two sides who have each averaged around ten shots a game or fewer, and Jiménez's own words about Cádiz's lack of attacking volume point the same way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. I lean lower with the shots: Eibar have been blunt in recent league games and Cádiz arrive without two regulars, with Antoñito, their top scorer, carrying most of the threat.
